title: Your resident Just in Time expert here to weigh in on the most recent...
transcript: I wanna talk about the race blind casting of real people. And specifically the casting of Nic Christopher as Bobby Darin in just in time. And I do believe that this is a very complex issue that really needs to be reviewed on a case by case basis. But in general, I have two rules of them. The first is kind of obvious, which is if the race was important to the real life person or the story that is being told, it should be cast as authentically as possible. Right. Like, for example, you're not gonna cast a white guy as Michael Jackson. Because his blackness is so important to his history and is actively discussed in the show. But the second, and perhaps less obvious rule of thumb comes down to how the show itself is framed. And this is where, for me, just in time enters the conversation. Because if you've never seen just in time, the actor playing Bobby Darin actually begins the show as themselves. And so when Nic Christopher is in the show, the announcer at the start of the show will say, ladies and gentlemen, please welcome to the stage Nic Christopher. And he'll come out, he'll sing some Bobby Darin tunes. He'll talk a little bit about himself and his upbringing and his connection to Bobby Darin, why he feels drawn to telling this story. It's not until about 20 minutes into the show that he actually starts performing as Bobby Darin. And even then, the actors playing Bobby Darin typically are not doing Bobby Darin impressions. They're basically playing a variation of themselves through the lens of Bobby Darin. And that's what I think makes this role so unique. That you don't get in a lot of bio-jukebox musicals. Where I truly think that this role could be played by anyone. Any age, ethnicity, gender, it really doesn't matter. Because they are coming out at the top of the show and saying, this is not Bobby Darin. And in fairness, I do think it helps that we have some amount of distance from Bobby Darin. To the point where a lot of us don't really know what he looked like or sounded like. He is not one of those people like Michael Jackson or Cher or Carole King. That have a very specific look and sound associated with them. And in fairness, I'm sure there are people out there that love Bobby Darin and Wanna see his songs and his life recreated as faithfully as possible. But I honestly don't think that those people would even like just in time to begin with. Because that's never been what it's about.
